title_clean: It really works! But you need to give it time
body_clean: I was initially skeptical if this would even work. We all know that with topical collagen products, your skin isn’t actually benefiting from the collagen… but what I loved were the peptides and HA. And mostly positive reviews. And it was on sale. So I thought why not. It took about 2 weeks for me to notice suddenly that my under eyes looked a lot better and I looked brighter and younger. Less tired. Also more plump and the wrinkles aren’t as deep. And my sleep has been the same. Hydration the same. Pretty much everything else the same. What I do: which I highly recommend. I press the applicator button ever so slightly (not all the way, that’s too much product for one use & you’re going to waste it) just so it starts to come out a tiny bit and I dab some on both under eyes, then I dab some on both eyelids. Yes, EYE LIDS. That’s also been a game changer. I was struggling with dry eyelids and this really has helped with that a lot. Then I roll it around lightly on all the areas I just dabbed the product onto. Then- this is important too, after I’ve given the product time to absorb and do its thing for at least a few minutes, I make sure to still moisturize on those areas. Bc think of it this way- do you just put your serums like HA or whatnot on your face and skip moisturizing? The serums aren’t enough. It might seem like it is initially, but then over time you’ll realize you’re really dry. So, TLDR, it showed results in 2 weeks, a little goes a long way, use it on your eyelids too, and don’t forget to moisturize after!

title_clean: Great budget choice for an eye serum but not ideal for sensitve skin
body_clean: I'm a 54 with thin, dry, crepey skin around my eyes. This is a pretty good lightweight niacinamide eye serum, especially for the price. It absorbs quickly, feels a little bit cooling when you use the applicator, and has a slight smoothing effect temporarily. Over time, the 2% niacinamide would likely help even out skin tone around the eye area - if you can tolerate it. This might not be a great choice for people with reactive or sensitive skin. Axis-y's sensitivity "clinical" test is a little bit misleading. It looks like it was a test panel with only 34 participants, which is a pretty small group. Niacinamide at 2%, botanical extracts, as well as papaya and other fruit extracts aren't great for people with a very sensitive eye area or allergies. I don't have particularly sensitive skin, even around my eyes, but it still caused temporary flushing. - Effectiveness: The peptides and niacinamide are definitely high enough on the list to see some benefit. I only used it a few weeks, but I could tell it was at least temporarily smoothing my under-eye a little bit. - Consistency: Thin serum that absorbs quickly, non-greasy. - Fragrance: none - Moisturizing/Hydrating: I didn't find this to be nearly hydrating or moisturizing enough for my dry skin and needed an eye cream over it. - Value for the money: $12 is a good price if it works for you, though it's only 0.33 ounces which is less than the standard 0.5 oz most eye products sell. I'm not using it on my eyes anymore, but I am using it up on my neck and chest where I need a little more help with hyper-pigmentation. To me, the formula is better for that than as an eye serum. Too bad the tube is so small.
